DEFECTS: CRITICAL: LANTERN changes from an open cylindrical cage containing a smaller glass globe to a substantially larger closed sphere. This is an object and silhouette replacement, not one material change on the same geometry.

MAJOR: LANTERN_BEFORE has nearly featureless black framing and synthetic glass; AFTER reads as a uniformly emissive ribbed sphere rather than photographed paper. Its black block base, missing visible support seams and uniform glow do not match the approved lantern.

MAJOR: WOOL_BEFORE reads as a smooth molded sheet; AFTER adds only fine surface texture without convincing wool fibers, pile, thickness or textile edge detail. Neither reproduces the approved blanket's shaggy, draped character.

MAJOR: WOOL preserves framing and silhouette, but the subtle color and surface change does not clearly communicate a distinct wool design state. Dark exposure and weak texture visibility undermine detail inspection.

MAJOR: OAK preserves drawer and handle alignment, but BEFORE has flat, broadly mapped grain and AFTER mainly darkens it, obscuring finish detail. The slab-like drawer construction and oversized grain do not convincingly match the approved dresser's framed fronts and richer wood appearance.

MAJOR: GLASS preserves the mullion and exterior alignment, but the change reads primarily as blur versus sharpness. BEFORE's diffuse orange patch becomes a sharply bounded, flat-looking lantern reflection in AFTER; neither state provides convincing glass-surface detail or an unambiguous physical design change.

MAJOR: ROOM_MATCH fails across the set: LANTERN and GLASS use brighter cyan-blue exterior tones than the approved deep-navy evening view; WOOL has muddy brown lighting and a simplified bed presentation; OAK lacks the approved dresser's tonal depth and construction cues. The closeups collectively read as a separate rendered scene rather than details photographed in the approved bedroom.
